job: Take a reason and commit a decision with buttons named for their effect.
purpose: A form with a line saying what each button does, a reason field with a word budget, the primary button named for its effect and a Decline that needs the reason too. It checks the reason, then fires fd:commit, or holds it first with data-fd-hold: inline, or in a toast with data-fd-hold-in="toast" so a queue can move on. A visible fd-commit-lock disables the buttons and says who can decide.
useWhen: A decision needs a reason that someone reads later: the audit log, the requester, the agent.
Approve and decline are both real answers and both need a why.
The viewer can read the case but not decide it, and must learn who can.

avoidWhen.when: A yes or no with nothing to record, such as dismissing a tip.
The action destroys something with history and needs the name typed.
A general form that edits a record.

states.name: invalid
states.how: aria-invalid="true" on the textarea and the fd-field-error shown, when the reason is missing or outside its budget

states.name: locked
states.how: a visible fd-commit-lock; the commit buttons are disabled and described by it

states.name: held
states.how: data-state="held" while a hold runs; the actions give way to fd-hold

states.name: committed
states.how: data-state="committed" once sent; reopen(form) undoes it after a failed send

variants.useWhen: Sending is hard to take back: hold the commit this many seconds with Undo.
The page moves on after a commit (a queue): hold it in a toast instead of in the form.

parts.role: The form (or a div inside another form).
One line on what each button does.
The word count against data-min-words and data-max-words.
The commit buttons: type="submit" with a value and data-verb.
Who can decide, when this viewer cannot.

keyboard.does: On a commit button: checks the reason, then commits or starts the hold.
While the hold runs: stops it and opens the form again.
